app.name: Next Rating
app.tagline: Predicts your next PDGA rating update from your rated rounds, including new rounds with unofficial round ratings and ratings you add yourself.
app.unofficial: Unofficial tool, not affiliated with or endorsed by the PDGA (Professional Disc Golf Association).
app.privacy: Your data stays in this browser. Nothing is sent to any server.

setup.title: Install the bookmarklet
setup.intro: The bookmarklet is a bookmark that reads your rounds on pdga.com and brings them here. Install it once in each browser you use.
setup.reads: It only reads the page you run it on and a few related pdga.com pages, never cookies, passwords or form fields.

setup.copied: Copied. Now follow the steps for your browser.
setup.iphone.title: Safari on iPhone
setup.iphone.bookmark: Tap Share (the square with an arrow), then Add Bookmark. Name it Next Rating and tap Save.
setup.iphone.pasteTitle: Paste the code as its address.
setup.iphone.paste: Tap Bookmarks (the book icon), then Edit, then Next Rating. Clear the address, paste the code and tap Done.
setup.iphone.run: Open your ratings details on pdga.com, then open Bookmarks and tap Next Rating.
setup.android.title: Chrome on Android
setup.android.pasteTitle: Paste the code as its URL.
setup.android.paste: Tap ⋮, then Bookmarks. Tap ⋮ next to the new bookmark, then Edit. Name it Next Rating and replace the URL with the code.
setup.android.run: Open your ratings details on pdga.com, tap the address bar and type Next Rating. Tap the bookmark among the suggestions: opening it from the bookmarks list does not run it.
setup.computer.title: Desktop browsers
setup.computer.bookmarkTitle: Add a bookmark with the code as its URL.
setup.computer.bookmark: Show the bookmarks bar (Ctrl+Shift+B, or Cmd+Shift+B on a Mac). Right-click it, choose to add a page or bookmark, name it Next Rating and paste the code as its URL.
setup.computer.run: Open your ratings details on pdga.com and click Next Rating in the bookmarks bar.
setup.tryResult: You come back here with your rounds and the message "Import complete."
setup.trouble.title: If it doesn't work
setup.trouble.address: Check that the bookmark's address starts with javascript: and holds the whole code. If not, copy and paste it again.
setup.trouble.browsers: Install it in each browser you use.
setup.trouble.homeScreen: The home screen icon opens the app in a normal browser tab, so the bookmarklet works from there too.
setup.trouble.check: If pdga.com shows a browser check, finish it, then run the bookmarklet again.
guide.title: How it works
guide.about.title: What the app does
guide.about.text: Next Rating predicts a player's next PDGA rating update from their rated rounds: official rounds, new rounds with unofficial round ratings, and round ratings you add yourself. It never calculates a round rating from a score.
guide.data.title: Where the data comes from
guide.data.bookmarklet: A bookmarklet reads the player's pages on pdga.com in your own browser, while you are on pdga.com, and brings what it read back here. The app has no server and fetches nothing from pdga.com itself.
guide.data.device: Everything stays in this browser on this device: players, imports, manual rounds and settings. Nothing is sent anywhere.
guide.rules.title: How a PDGA rating is calculated
guide.rules.intro: The app follows the {guide}, plus a clarification from the PDGA Ratings team:
guide.rules.window: Window: the rounds from the 12 months up to the player's most recent rated round. With fewer than 8 rounds in that window, 24 months.
guide.rules.drop: Low rounds are dropped: each round in the window is compared with the average and standard deviation of the other rounds in the window, and dropped when it is more than 100 points or more than 2.5 standard deviations below that average. This needs at least 7 rounds in the window.
guide.rules.double: Double weighting: with at least 9 counted rounds, the most recent quarter of them (rounded up) count twice. When that boundary falls inside an event, the highest rated rounds of that event are the ones that count twice.
guide.rules.holes: Hole count: a round shorter than 18 holes counts for its share of 18, so a 9-hole round counts half. A longer round counts as one round.
guide.rules.result: The rating is the weighted average of the counted rounds, rounded to a whole number. The app works this out again from all rounds instead of trusting PDGA's own flags, since a round dropped before can count again once new rounds arrive.
guide.rules.noNew: A rating only changes when new rated rounds are added. So when no unofficial or manual round counts in the next update, the prediction is the official rating, even if the app's own calculation from the rounds on pdga.com would round to another number.
guide.rules.verified: These rules are checked against the official ratings, and the rounds PDGA counted, of real players, including two low rounds dropped in the same window. One thing is not yet checked against a real player: the weighting of rounds shorter than 18 holes.
guide.rules.decimals: The calculated official rating next to the official one, such as 977.65, comes from the whole round ratings shown on pdga.com. PDGA's own calculation may use decimals that the pages do not show, so its unrounded value can differ a little.
guide.rounds.title: Official, unofficial and manual rounds
guide.rounds.official: Official rounds come from the player's ratings details on pdga.com. The report deadline does not apply to them.
guide.rounds.unofficial: Unofficial rounds come from event results that are not rated officially yet. PDGA shows unofficial round ratings there, and they can still change a little when the event becomes official.
guide.rounds.manual: Manual rounds are the ones you add yourself under Add a round, for example a round you expect to play at an upcoming event. They stay on this device.
guide.rounds.deadline: Ratings are updated on the second Tuesday of each month and count events reported by the Sunday before ({rule}). Unofficial and manual rounds from events after that deadline count in the following update, and the round list says so.
guide.rounds.ruleLink: when ratings are updated, on pdga.com
guide.xtier.title: Events the next update may not count
guide.xtier.choose: Unofficial rounds count in the prediction by default, but the next update may leave out an event. Under Rounds you can uncheck any unofficial event with one tap, and Why it changed then says what counting it would give. The choice is stored for each player on this device. There are three cases:
guide.xtier.late: A late report. The app goes by the event's date, but an update counts only events reported by its deadline. When an event's report arrives after the deadline, it counts in the following update instead. Nothing on pdga.com shows this in advance, so these events have no mark.
guide.xtier.league: An unfinished league. A league (tier L on pdga.com) counts only when the whole league is finished and reported, so its first weeks can show unofficial ratings that no update counts yet. Its rounds are marked "League: counts only when the whole league is finished and reported".
guide.xtier.rule: An X-tier event PDGA leaves out. X-tier (the tiers XA, XB, XC and XM on pdga.com) are events outside the usual tiers. Under section 5.10 of PDGA's Competition Manual, X-tier events with non-standard rules, such as mulligans, can still produce round ratings, but those ratings do not count in player ratings. Other X-tier events, such as ones with restricted eligibility or charity payouts, are rated and count like any other event. Which kind an event is shows only once it is rated, so its unofficial rounds count, marked "X-tier: may not count".
guide.xtier.tier: The league and X-tier marks come from the event's tier on the player's profile page on pdga.com.
guide.xtier.official: For official rounds the app follows PDGA's own flags: a round PDGA did not evaluate although it is dated inside the window PDGA used never counts, also after new rounds move the window. The round list shows it as "Not counted by PDGA".
guide.xtier.top8: The Top 8 still counts these rounds, since they are rated rounds.
guide.why.title: Why it changed
guide.why.compare: Why it changed compares the last official update with the prediction. It starts from the rounds PDGA counted and lists what differs: new rounds, and rounds that left the window, started or stopped counting twice, or were dropped or brought back.
guide.why.net: Each line shows how many points it moves the unrounded prediction. The net total at the top says what the lines add up to and what that rounds to. Many lines can cancel out: a new round can move the window so that old rounds leave it and others start or stop counting twice, while the rounded rating stays the same.
guide.why.difference: If the rounds PDGA counted do not give the official rating, a line "Difference from PDGA's last calculation" makes the lines add up to the change shown. Without new rated rounds there is nothing to explain: it says that the rating stays.
guide.chart.title: The rating chart
guide.chart.points: The Chart card draws each rated round as a point, newest to the right. The shape shows where the round comes from: a circle for an official round, a square for an unofficial one and a triangle for your own. The fill shows what the next update does with it: filled counts, a ring around it counts twice, and hollow does not count, because it is outside the window or after the report deadline. A cross in a hollow point marks a round dropped as an outlier, left out by you or not counted by PDGA.
guide.chart.lines: The shaded area is the window the prediction uses. Across it, the dashed line is the official rating and the solid line the prediction; when they are equal, one line shows the value once. Both are today's values, so a period that does not reach the window leaves them out. For the official rating after each past update, the link under the chart opens the player's ratings history on pdga.com.
guide.chart.read: Tap a point to see its round, or show the rounds as a table. The period is the last 24 months by default, ending at a planned round of your own if it is later than today. Like the Top 8, it can also be a year, the rating window or a custom range.
guide.target.title: Reach a target rating
guide.target.how: The target calculator finds the average round rating your next rounds need to reach a rating at the update they count in. It adds that many 18-hole rounds on the date you pick (today unless you change it) and runs the same calculation as the prediction, so the window, dropped rounds and double weighting all apply.
guide.target.answers: It also says when the target is already reached and what keeps it there, or when even rounds rated 1150 would not reach it. The date decides the update: the first one whose report deadline is on or after it, so a date on the Monday or Tuesday of update week counts in the following update. The new rounds are the newest, so the date also ends the 12-month window, and the answer lists the rounds that leave it.
guide.top8.title: Top 8 and the Global Masters Series
guide.top8.idea: The Top 8 card follows the idea of PDGA's {gms}: the 8 highest rated rounds of a period, with their sum, average and highest rating. Here it works for any player, and for a calendar year, the rating window or dates you choose.
guide.top8.rounds: Official and unofficial rounds count, also rounds the prediction drops or leaves out, with no hole weighting. DNF rounds do not count. Your own rounds, the ones you add by hand, count only when you tick Include my own rounds, and are marked Own.
